content.overview: Section 30 of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956 enables any Hindu to dispose of by will or other testamentary disposition any property which is capable of being so disposed of by him or her, in accordance with the provisions of the Indian Succession Act, 1925, or any other law applicable. The interest of a male Hindu in Mitakshara coparcenary property is expressly deemed to be property capable of being disposed of by him within the meaning of the section.
content.glance: Ask: (1) Hindu testator? (2) Property capable of testamentary disposition? (3) Coparcenary interest included for male Hindu? (4) Formalities under applicable succession law?
content.study:
Section 30 removes older doubts about the power of a Hindu to bequeath property, including Mitakshara coparcenary interest of a male Hindu, which is deemed capable of testamentary disposition.

The will must satisfy the formalities and capacity rules of the Indian Succession Act, 1925 (or other applicable law).

Intestate rules under the HSA apply only to the extent property is not validly disposed of by will.

No case holdings invented. Case-law verification remains a separate gate.

sections.heading: Testamentary power
sections.body: Any Hindu may dispose by will of property capable of testamentary disposition.

sections.heading: Coparcenary interest
sections.body: Male Hindu’s interest in Mitakshara coparcenary property is deemed capable of being disposed of by him under s. 30.

sections.heading: Governing formalities
sections.body: Indian Succession Act, 1925 (or other applicable law) supplies capacity and execution rules.

sections.heading: Relation to intestacy
sections.body: HSA intestate provisions apply to the undisposed residue.

sections.heading: Female testators
sections.body: Female Hindus may also dispose by will of property they hold as absolute owners (including under s. 14).

examples.title: Will of coparcenary interest
examples.body: Male Hindu executes a valid will disposing of his Mitakshara interest — permitted under s. 30 explanation/deeming language.

hypotheticals.question: Does s. 30 create a new form of will?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. It enables disposition of capable property; formalities remain those of the applicable succession law.

distinctions.title: Testamentary (s. 30) vs intestate (ss. 8/15)
distinctions.right: Intestate rules apply to undisposed property.

misconceptions.trap: A Hindu cannot bequeath Mitakshara coparcenary interest.
misconceptions.correction: Section 30 deems a male Hindu’s Mitakshara interest capable of testamentary disposition.
